summary: This program is the bakery's entry point: it creates one plain Cookie and one DecoratedCookie, then prints the description each object gives of itself. It shows how a subclass can answer the same describe() message differently from its parent.

lines.text: The application class that ties the domain classes together; it holds behavior rather than data, so it has no fields of its own.
Execution starts here when you run the program, which is why the sample objects are created inside this method.
Calls the Cookie constructor with a flavor, producing one concrete cookie object whose flavor is stored inside it.
Creates an object of the subclass; because DecoratedCookie extends Cookie, it inherits the flavor handling and adds decoration behavior.
Asks the plain cookie to describe itself, so the printing happens here while the wording lives in the Cookie class.
The same method name on the decorated cookie runs the subclass's overridden version, which is polymorphism in action.
